tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal Stack Ordering
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The final configuration on the goal peg must be a descending stack: the largest disk at the bottom and each higher disk must be smaller than the one below it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Use when checking whether the target arrangement is valid or when planning which disk can be placed next on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: For a goal of [5,4,3,2,1] (bottom‑to‑top), any state where a smaller disk lies below a larger one is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place Larger Disks Before Smaller
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Because a larger disk can never sit on a smaller one, any disk that must appear below another in the final stack must be moved onto the goal peg before the smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding the order of moves toward the goal, schedule moves of larger disks earlier than moves of the smaller disks that will sit on them.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 5 onto the goal peg before moving disk 4, since 4 must end up on top of 5.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free Blocked Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A disk that has any smaller disks on top cannot be moved directly; you must first relocate those smaller disks to other pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the disk you need to move is not the topmost disk on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 5 is under disk 2 on peg 0, move disk 2 elsewhere before moving disk 5.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Auxiliary Peg for Temporary Storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: In a three‑peg problem, the peg that is neither the source nor the destination of a move serves as a temporary holding place for displaced disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to clear a peg or hold a disk while moving another, choose the third peg as the buffer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: When moving disk 5 from peg 0 to peg 2, store the smaller blocking disks on peg 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Sub‑tower Transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Moving a stack of k disks from one peg to another follows the recursion: first move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the k‑th disk to the destination, and finally move the k‑1 disks onto the k‑th disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous block of disks while preserving their internal order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disks 1‑3 from peg 0 to peg 2, first move disks 1‑2 to peg 1, move disk 3 to peg 2, then move disks 1‑2 onto peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Check Move Legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A legal move must take the topmost disk from the source peg and place it onto a destination peg whose top disk is larger (or the destination is empty).
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before committing any move, verify both source and destination constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top is disk 2 is illegal because 3 > 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate Final Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After writing a complete move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to ensure that the final configuration exactly matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have finished constructing the move sequence, before submitting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Step through the 21 moves and confirm that peg 2 ends as [5,4,3,2,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Maintain 0‑Indexed Peg Numbers
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The output format expects peg identifiers 0, 1, 2; using any other numbering (e.g., 1‑based) will be rejected.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the move list, always label pegs with 0‑based indices.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Write [1, 2, 0] to move disk 1 from peg 2 to peg 0, not [1, 3, 1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track Current Top Disk on Each Peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keep an up‑to‑date mental (or written) record of the topmost disk on every peg after each move, so you never attempt to move a non‑top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the construction of the move sequence, after each move update the top‑disk record.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 2 from peg 0 to peg 1, the new top of peg 0 is disk 5.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Leverage Existing Larger Disks on Target as Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains larger disks that are correctly placed, you can place a smaller disk directly onto them, using the existing stack as a base.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the destination peg already holds part of the final stack, treat those disks as immutable foundations for subsequent moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 5 onto peg 2, you can place disk 4 onto peg 2 because 5 > 4.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving the required disk without checking the size of the top disk on the destination peg, violating the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the moving disk's size with the destination peg's top disk; proceed only if the destination is empty or its top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model can forget that only the topmost disk on a peg is movable, especially when a disk is blocked by smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain a record of the current top disk on each peg and restrict moves to those disks.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely placing a small disk on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to fill the goal peg early, overlooking that larger disks still need to be placed beneath the small one.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Follow the 'Place Larger Disks Before Smaller' principle; only place a small disk on the goal after all larger disks that belong below it are already positioned.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Confusion between 0‑based and 1‑based numbering leads to wrong peg identifiers in the output.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always use 0‑based indices (0, 1, 2) when writing moves; double‑check each move's peg numbers before finalizing.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Skipping final verification of the goal state
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the move list is correct without replaying it, missing subtle errors.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After constructing the move list, simulate the entire sequence from the initial configuration and confirm that the final arrangement matches the goal exactly.
